examples.ko: 어느 맑은 가을날에 가족과 함께 산에 갔어요.
examples.en: On a clear autumn day, I went to the mountains with my family.
The afternoon sunlight of an autumn day is so warm.

examples.ko: 오늘처럼 시원한 가을날이면 밖에 나가고 싶어요.
examples.en: On a cool autumn day like today, I want to go outside.

examples.ko: 가을날엔 낙엽 밟는 소리가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: On autumn days, I really like the sound of stepping on fallen leaves.

examples.ko: 비 오는 가을날은 왠지 마음이 쓸쓸해요.
examples.en: A rainy autumn day somehow makes me feel lonely.
I kept the autumn day I spent with friends in photos.

explain: '가을철'이 가을이라는 기간을 말한다면 '가을날'은 가을의 어느 하루와 그날의 분위기를 말해요. 같은 식으로 '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'도 써요. '어느 가을날'처럼 이야기를 시작할 때 자주 어울려요.

phrases.en: One autumn day, I met an old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 시작할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for opening a story.

phrases.example: 비 오는 가을날에는 따뜻한 차가 생각나요.
phrases.en: On a rainy autumn day, I think of warm tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨를 앞에 붙여 그날의 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the weather before it to set the mood of that day.

phrases.en: On an autumn morning, the air is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하루 중 때를 뒤에 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can add a time of day after it.

explain_en: While '가을철' refers to the autumn period, '가을날' refers to a single autumn day and its atmosphere. In the same way you can say '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'. It works well for starting a story, as in '어느 가을날' (one autumn day).

examples.en: The autumn breeze is blowing, so it's perfect for a walk.
I walked slowly along the river in the autumn breeze.
Leaves fall one by one in the autumn wind.
The autumn breeze is cool, but it gets a bit cold in the evening.
I opened the window and heard the sound of the autumn wind.
I listened to a song as refreshing as an autumn breeze.

explain: 선선하고 시원한 느낌이 먼저 떠올라서 '가을바람이 불다', '선선한 가을바람'처럼 자주 써요. 차갑게 세게 부는 '찬바람'과는 느낌이 달라요. 노래나 글에서는 쓸쓸한 마음을 말할 때도 나와요.

phrases.en: The cool autumn breeze feels nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시원한 느낌을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the cool, fresh feeling.

phrases.en: When I open the window, the autumn breeze blows in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 부는 것을 말하는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say the wind is blowing.

phrases.en: I enjoyed the autumn breeze in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 나가서 바람을 즐긴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of going outside to enjoy the breeze.
phrases.en_equiv: to get some fresh autumn air

explain_en: It first brings to mind a cool, pleasant feeling, so it is often used as '가을바람이 불다' or '선선한 가을바람'. It feels different from '찬바람' (cold wind), which is harsher. In songs and writing it can also express a lonely mood.

examples.en: I got earrings as a birthday present.
My earring fell off and I searched for it for a long time.
There is a small gem set in the earrings.
The right earring is missing.
I bought both the earrings and the necklace as a set.

examples.ko: 이 귀고리는 가벼워서 오래 해도 편해요.
examples.en: These earrings are light, so they're comfortable even after a long time.

explain: '귀걸이'라고도 하며 일상에서 두 말을 다 써요. 동사는 '귀고리를 하다', '귀고리를 끼다/달다'처럼 말하고, 한 쪽은 '한 짝'이라고 세요. 귀에 하는 장식이니 '목걸이, 팔찌'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I bought new earrings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀고리'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 둘 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 귀고리; both are used in daily speech.

phrases.en: Today I'm wearing big earrings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장식을 몸에 한다고 할 때 '하다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 하다 is commonly used for wearing accessories.

phrases.en: I lost one earring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘 중 하나를 셀 때 '짝'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 짝 counts one of a pair.

explain_en: It is also called '귀걸이', and both words are used in daily life. You say '귀고리를 하다' or '귀고리를 끼다/달다', and one earring is counted as '한 짝'. It helps to learn it together with '목걸이' and '팔찌'.

examples.en: Maple leaves turn red in autumn.
I picked up the colored leaves that had fallen on the road.
I pressed a colored leaf between the pages of a book to dry it.
I received maple-leaf-shaped cookies as a gift.
When the wind blew, the colored leaves fell in a shower.
The child made a picture out of colored leaves.

explain: '단풍'은 가을에 색이 변한 잎 전체를 말하고, '단풍잎'은 잎 한 장 한 장을 가리켜요. 나무가 물드는 건 '단풍이 들다'라고 하고, '단풍 구경'을 가요. 발음은 [단풍닙]이에요.

phrases.en: The mountain has turned autumn colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을에 잎 색이 변할 때 쓰는 말로, '단풍잎'보다 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when leaves change color in autumn, referring to the whole scene.

phrases.en: On the weekend I went to see the autumn leaves with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 나들이를 갈 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for autumn outings.

phrases.en: I picked up pretty autumn leaves in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어진 잎 한 장을 집을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for picking up a fallen leaf.
phrases.en_equiv: to pick up an autumn leaf

explain_en: '단풍' refers to the autumn colors as a whole, while '단풍잎' points to the individual leaves. The color change is '단풍이 들다', and people go on '단풍 구경' trips. The pronunciation is [단풍닙].

examples.en: My lips were dry, so I put on a little lip gloss.
With lip gloss, your lips look moist.
This lip gloss isn't sticky.
I even have two lip glosses in my bag.

examples.ko: 립글로스 색깔이 너무 진한 것 같아요.
examples.en: The lip gloss color seems too dark.
I made my lips shiny with lip gloss.

explain: 입술에 윤기를 주는 화장품이에요. 색을 진하게 내는 '립스틱'과 달리 반짝이는 느낌을 줄 때 자주 말해요. 입술에 '바르다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I put on lip gloss before going out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입술에 화장품을 '바르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 바르다 (to apply) for lip products.

phrases.en: Clear lip gloss has no color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 없고 반짝이는 느낌만 줄 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say this for gloss with no color that only adds shine.

phrases.en: I use lip gloss instead of lipstick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 진한 입술 화장품이라서 립글로스와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lip product with strong color, used to compare with lip gloss.

explain_en: It is a cosmetic that gives the lips a glossy look. Unlike '립스틱', which is for strong color, it is often mentioned for a shiny finish. It goes with the verb '바르다' (to apply).

examples.en: Spring rain fell and the flowers got prettier.

examples.ko: 봄비 오는 날에는 따뜻한 차가 생각나요.
examples.en: On days with spring rain, I think of warm tea.

examples.ko: 우산 없이 봄비를 맞고 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly in the spring rain without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 봄비는 겨우내 굳어 있던 땅을 적시고 새싹들을 돋아나게 해요.
examples.en: Spring rain soaks the ground that was hardened all winter and makes new sprouts come up.

examples.ko: 이번 봄비는 하루 종일 조용히 내렸어요.
examples.en: This spring rain fell quietly all day.

examples.ko: 봄비에 젖은 꽃잎이 길에 떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: Petals soaked by the spring rain lie on the road.

explain: '봄비'는 노래와 시에서 자주 나와서 감성적인 느낌이 있어요. '봄비가 내리다', '봄비를 맞다'처럼 써요. '여름비, 가을비, 겨울비'처럼 계절 이름을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Spring rain has been falling since morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 오는 모습을 조금 감성적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly poetic way to say that rain is falling.

phrases.en: I had no umbrella, so I walked in the spring rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비를 그대로 맞는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting rained on without cover.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in spring rain

phrases.en: The petals fell in the spring rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 봄비 때문에 생긴 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에 says what happened because of the spring rain.

explain_en: 봄비 shows up often in songs and poems, so it has a sentimental feel. Say '봄비가 내리다' or '봄비를 맞다'. You can also say 여름비, 가을비 and 겨울비 the same way.

examples.ko: 오늘은 정말 더운 여름날이라 에어컨을 하루 종일 켰어요.
examples.en: Today is a really hot summer day, so I kept the air conditioner on all day.
One summer evening I took a walk with a friend.
A summer shower pours down suddenly.

examples.ko: 여름날 아침에는 일찍 일어나는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On summer mornings it's good to get up early.

examples.ko: 여름날 바닷가에서 보낸 하루를 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the day I spent at the beach in summer.

examples.ko: 비 오는 여름날에는 집에서 영화를 봐요.
examples.en: On rainy summer days I watch movies at home.

explain: '여름'은 계절 이름이고, '여름날'은 여름의 어느 하루나 여름다운 날씨를 말할 때 써요. 이야기나 노래에서 '어느 여름날'로 시작하는 말이 많아요. '봄날', '겨울날'도 같은 방식으로 써요.

phrases.example: 어느 여름날 아침에 갑자기 비가 왔어요.
phrases.en: One summer morning, it suddenly rained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 시작할 때 '어느'를 붙여 정확한 날짜 없이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 어느 starts a story about a summer day without giving the exact date.

phrases.en: On hot summer days, watermelon tastes really good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨를 설명하는 말과 함께 여름의 하루를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with a weather word to describe a summer day.

phrases.en: I want to go to the sea with my family on a summer day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 여름의 어느 날에 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에 says what happens on a summer day.

explain_en: 여름 is the season, while 여름날 means a particular day in summer or a summery day. Stories and songs often open with '어느 여름날'. 봄날 and 겨울날 work the same way.

examples.ko: 학교 근처에 싼 월세방을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a cheap rented room near school.
At first I lived alone in a small rented room.

examples.ko: 월세방은 보증금이 적은 대신 매달 돈을 내야 해요.
examples.en: With a monthly-rent room, the deposit is small but you pay every month.
For a monthly-rent room, it's spacious and clean.
My goal is to move from a monthly-rent room to a jeonse house.

examples.ko: 지금 월세방에 살지만 곧 이사할 거예요.
examples.en: I live in a rented room now, but I'll move soon.

explain: '월세'는 매달 내는 집값이고 '전세'는 큰 보증금을 맡기고 사는 방식이라서 둘을 구분해서 말해요. '월세방'은 보통 작은 방이나 원룸처럼 혼자 사는 방을 떠올리게 해요. '월세방을 구하다', '월세방에 살다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a rented room near school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 찾을 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when searching for a place.

phrases.en: I'm living in a small rented room now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 사는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you currently live.

phrases.en: The monthly rent is 500,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방이 아니라 매달 내는 돈을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the monthly money, not the room.

explain_en: '월세' is rent paid monthly, while '전세' means leaving a large deposit to live in a place, so Koreans distinguish the two. '월세방' usually brings to mind a small room or studio for one person. Say '월세방을 구하다' (look for) or '월세방에 살다' (live in).

examples.ko: 하얀 웨딩드레스가 신부에게 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The white wedding dress suits the bride really well.

examples.ko: 친구는 웨딩드레스를 사지 않고 빌려서 입었어요.
examples.en: My friend rented her wedding dress instead of buying it.
The wedding dress my sister wore was really pretty.
We took a lot of photos at the wedding dress shop.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 웨딩드레스 대신 한복을 입을 거예요.
examples.en: I'll wear a hanbok instead of a wedding dress at the wedding.
I'm looking for shoes that go with the wedding dress.

explain: 서양식 결혼식 옷은 '웨딩드레스', 전통 결혼식 옷은 '한복'이라고 해요. 결혼식 전에 사진만 따로 찍는 것을 '웨딩 촬영'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The bride wore a wedding dress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는 행동에는 '입다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'ipda' for the action of wearing clothes.

phrases.en: I chose a wedding dress together with my mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼 준비를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about wedding preparation.

phrases.en: We had a wedding photo shoot before the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼식 전에 사진만 따로 찍는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A photo shoot taken separately before the wedding.

explain_en: The Western-style bridal gown is a 웨딩드레스, while traditional wedding clothes are a 한복. Taking wedding photos separately before the ceremony is called '웨딩 촬영'.

examples.en: This cafe has a really pretty interior.

examples.ko: 새집 인테리어를 어떻게 할지 고민하고 있어요.
examples.en: I am thinking about how to do the interior of my new home.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 인테리어 공사가 한 달이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The interior renovation of our shop took a whole month.

examples.ko: 저는 인테리어 사진을 보는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like looking at interior design photos.
I decided to go in after seeing the restaurant's interior.

examples.ko: 인테리어를 바꾸고 나서 집이 훨씬 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: After changing the interior, the house became much brighter.

explain: 집이나 가게를 새로 고칠 때 '인테리어를 하다'라고 자주 말해요. 공사까지 크게 하면 '인테리어 공사', 분위기를 칭찬할 때는 '인테리어가 예쁘다'라고 해요. '실내장식'이라는 말도 있지만 훨씬 딱딱해서 일상에서는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: I am redoing my home's interior this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 가게를 새로 고칠 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when renovating a home or shop.

phrases.en: This restaurant has pretty interior design.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공간의 분위기를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise the look of a space.

phrases.en: The shop's interior work takes a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 공사를 크게 할 때 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the work is actual construction.

explain_en: When fixing up a home or shop, Koreans often say '인테리어를 하다'. A big job is '인테리어 공사' (renovation work), and for praise you say '인테리어가 예쁘다'. The word '실내장식' exists but is much stiffer and rare in daily talk.

examples.ko: 책상 좌우에 작은 책꽂이를 하나씩 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put a small bookshelf on each side of the desk.
I arranged the books I've read on the shelf by date.

examples.ko: 책꽂이가 꽉 차서 새 책장을 사야 해요.
examples.en: The bookshelf is full, so I need to buy a new bookcase.
Dust flew up as I pulled a book off the shelf.

examples.ko: 책꽂이 맨 위 칸에는 사전을 꽂아 두었어요.
examples.en: I keep the dictionaries on the top shelf of the bookshelf.

examples.ko: 이 책꽂이는 벽에 걸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This bookshelf can be hung on the wall.

explain: '책장'은 보통 방에 놓는 큰 가구이고 '책꽂이'는 책상 위나 벽에 두는 작은 것을 말할 때가 많아요. 두 말을 바꿔 쓰기도 해요. '책을 꽂다', '책을 빼다'와 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I bought a big bookcase for my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. 보통 방에 놓는 큰 가구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word; usually a large piece of furniture for a room.

phrases.en: Put the books you've read back on the shelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 제자리에 넣을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for putting a book in its place.

phrases.en: I took one book off the bookshelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽂다'의 반대로, 책을 꺼낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '꽂다'; used when taking a book out.
phrases.en_equiv: to take a book from the shelf

explain_en: '책장' is usually a large piece of furniture in a room, while '책꽂이' often means a smaller one on a desk or wall. The two are sometimes used interchangeably. It helps to remember it with '책을 꽂다' (slot a book in) and '책을 빼다' (pull one out).

examples.en: I put a pin in my hair.
The pin fell out and my hair came down.
I attached a name tag to my clothes with a pin.
Could you lend me just one pin?
Small pins are easy to lose.
I pricked my finger on a pin and it hurts.

explain: 머리에 꽂는 건 '머리핀', 옷에 다는 건 '옷핀'이라고 해요. 작고 뾰족한 물건을 널리 가리키지만 압정은 '압정'이라고 따로 불러요. 지도 앱에서 위치를 표시할 때 '핀 찍다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I bought a hairpin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리에 꽂는 핀은 보통 '머리핀'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pin for the hair is usually called 머리핀.

phrases.en: I fixed my clothes in place with a safety pin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 잡아 주는 작은 핀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small pin that holds clothing in place.

phrases.en: Please drop a pin on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지도 앱에서 위치를 표시할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when marking a location in a map app.

explain_en: A pin for your hair is a 머리핀 and one for clothes is an 옷핀. It covers small pointed things broadly, but a thumbtack has its own word, 압정. On map apps, people say 핀 찍다 for marking a location.
